_comment: Multi-Cloud Portability Experiment v1. Controlled benchmark: Online Boutique. Infrastructure A: AWS EKS. Infrastructure B: GCP GKE.
_rationale: The capstone requires deploying the same benchmark application to two cloud providers using the same methodology and observing differences via CloudPort. This experiment uses Online Boutique (Google microservices demo) as the controlled benchmark workload, Locust for reproducible load generation, and the CloudPort multi-cloud inspector for infrastructure profiling. Provider differences (load balancer type, StorageClass provisioner, CNI, IAM model) are documented and classified as INFRASTRUCTURE_DIFFERENCE — they are not automatically classified as leakage. Application-visible measurements (request latency, error rate, throughput) are compared under the same load profile across repeated trials.
name: multicloud-portability-v1
description: Multi-cloud infrastructure portability experiment comparing Online Boutique performance on AWS EKS (Infrastructure A) vs GCP GKE (Infrastructure B) under the same Locust load profile. Measures application-visible differences to assess infrastructure leakage.

benchmark.invariant: IDENTICAL kustomization applied to both clusters — same manifests, same image tags

loadProfile.invariant: IDENTICAL load profile applied to both clusters in each trial

replication.description: 5 paired trials: AWS then GCP (or interleaved), same load profile per pair. Minimum 5 trials required by the statistical framework.

unavoidableDifferences.note: Different load balancer implementations. NOT automatically classified as leakage. Application-visible impact (latency, error rate) must be measured.
Different storage provisioners. Online Boutique uses Redis for cart (in-memory) — storage differences unlikely to be application-visible. Documented for completeness.
Different network data planes. May affect pod-to-pod latency. Application-visible impact must be measured.

unavoidableDifferences.gcp: e2-medium (2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM, custom Arm/x86)
unavoidableDifferences.note: Nominally equivalent node capacity. CPU architecture and memory subsystem differences are provider-specific and unavoidable.
Different identity mechanisms. Not application-visible for Online Boutique workloads.

statisticalFramework.note: The existing CloudPort statisticalTests.js is reused unchanged.

leakageFramework.note: Infrastructure differences are classified separately from application leakage. Leakage is only classified when the causal chain (infra diff → app measurement → repeated trials → statistical analysis) supports it.

hypotheses: The same Online Boutique workload under the same Locust load profile will exhibit measurable differences in request latency between AWS EKS and GCP GKE due to provider-specific load balancer and network data plane implementations.
Any latency difference will replicate consistently across 5 paired trials.
Infrastructure differences (load balancer type, CNI, StorageClass) are real and will be detected by the multi-cloud inspector — but do not automatically constitute application leakage.

successCriteria.note: With n=5, significant results require large effect sizes. Results reported honestly regardless of significance. No fabrication of measurements.
